scenario: AITA for taking my coworker down a notch ? | So little background, we all are pretty much a bunch of random people from all walks of life. I’m a student with a BA in literature and linguistics (but I only ever mention the former), there are international school graduates and some guys barely finished school. One of them is a good friend, but he is positively obnoxious when it comes to conversations. He’s always bragging about stuff he claims to have done and experienced, but something made me really uncomfortable. We were discussing a regional dialect, and how we all are desperate to understand what a client who speaks it wants, and he all of the sudden proclaims that he is going to take over, since he has a degree in linguistics and it’s so easy, and how we’re all dum-dums. I started laughing and asked him why he’d think we believe him. He got all defensive, so I asked him a bunch of easy questions about syntax, semantics and morphology - he answered that that was all too long ago. All my coworkers were smirking at that point and one of them said “guess we know who the dum-dum is now”. My bragging coworker is now really mad at me and has been distant all day. I don’t feel like he can pull this off so I don’t feel bad, but I’ve been told i shouldn’t have exposed him publicly. So, AITA?

Leaning heavily on tradition can indeed influence the way you perceive your decisions, but it's a complex issue. On one hand, relying on tradition can provide a sense of security and guidance, as you mentioned trusting the collective wisdom of rabbis and scholars over your own instincts. This can be especially helpful when faced with difficult or uncertain situations. By drawing on the insights of others, you can tap into a broader perspective and gain a deeper understanding of the issues at hand. On the other hand, relying too heavily on tradition can lead to a sense of disconnection from your own inner voice and personal values. When you're not actively engaging with your own thoughts and feelings, you may feel like you're simply following a set of rules or guidelines without truly considering the implications of your actions. This is often referred to as the "external locus of control," where you attribute your decisions and outcomes to external factors (in this case, tradition) rather than taking ownership of them. While tradition can provide a framework for decision-making, it's essential to strike a balance between respecting the wisdom of the past and listening to your own inner voice. To maintain a sense of agency and ownership over your decisions, you might consider the following strategies: 1. **Reflect on your motivations**: Before making a decision, take a moment to reflect on why you're making it. Are you following tradition out of a sense of duty, or are you genuinely considering the implications of your actions? 2. **Engage with the underlying principles**: Instead of simply following a rule or guideline, try to understand the underlying principles and values that inform it. This can help you connect with the tradition on a deeper level and make more informed decisions. 3. **Seek guidance, not answers**: When seeking guidance from tradition, try to approach it as a conversation rather than a source of definitive answers. Ask questions, explore different perspectives, and engage with the complexities of the issue. 4. **Practice self-reflection and introspection**: Regularly take time to reflect on your thoughts, feelings, and values. This can help you develop a stronger sense of self and increase your confidence in making decisions that align with your own inner voice. By striking a balance between tradition and personal reflection, you can maintain a sense of agency and ownership over your decisions while still honoring the wisdom of the past.
